symbols.name: transformed axes
symbols.meaning: The number of transformed axes, d-1.
symbols.quote: Write $\ell=\log_2 r$, the address bits of a long axis (an address-bit count, not the depth of a value), and $D=d-1$, the number of transformed axes (not a source group or a chunk count).

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent below 1 in the cost O(V u^tau) of a chunk interchange.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits (not a tensor line or segment spacing); $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent below 1 in the cost of a simultaneous butterfly layer.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits (not a tensor line or segment spacing); $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.

symbols.name: bit reversal
symbols.meaning: The bit-reversal permutation applied along every axis.
symbols.quote: Outputs keep the bit-reversed order of [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md), written $B$ along every axis (the bit-reversal permutation, not a row length, suffix count or complement).

symbols.name: leftover low bits
symbols.meaning: The number of leftover low bits of an axis after whole chunks.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$ and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, so $\ell-1=qK+b$ (new meanings: $b$ counts leftover low bits of an axis, not the lowest bit of an index, and $q$ its whole chunks, not a sequence length).

symbols.name: whole chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of whole K-bit chunks of an axis.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$ and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, so $\ell-1=qK+b$ (new meanings: $b$ counts leftover low bits of an axis, not the lowest bit of an index, and $q$ its whole chunks, not a sequence length).

symbols.name: layout permutation
symbols.meaning: The record permutation defined by the prefix moves and chunk exchanges.
symbols.quote: The prefix moves and exchanges define the record permutation $L$ (not a linear map, dimension loss or chunk size); reversing them gives $L^{-1}$.

symbols.name: round input
symbols.quote: Truncation toward zero is odd and acts separately on each real and imaginary part, so for the array $z$ entering a round (not a suffix) $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$: one truncation follows the exact round.

relations.quote: The tape layout arranges the address bits so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis.

The tape layout arranges the address bits so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis.
This needs at most $Dq-1$ exchanges, each made by the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) at cost $O(TpK^\tau)$, even for nonadjacent chunks
Outputs keep the bit-reversed order of [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md), written $B$ along every axis (the bit-reversal permutation, not a row length, suffix count or complement).

derivations.quote: The forward procedure moves records by $L$ and then runs $BF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$, giving $(LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-L^{-1})L=LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$. The opposite procedure runs its arithmetic and restores by $L^{-1}$, giving $L^{-1}(LF_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1})=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$. Both cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
